title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 12

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will students practise the email format?
tasks.audioText: The engineering office has introduced a standard format for technical emails. The template includes a clear subject line, the component reference and a short description of the issue. Students will practise using it on Tuesday at eleven in the computer room. They should bring the sample drawing from the previous lesson.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which document should they bring?
tasks.audioText: The engineering office has introduced a standard format for technical emails. The template includes a clear subject line, the component reference and a short description of the issue. Students will practise using it on Tuesday at eleven in the computer room. They should bring the sample drawing from the previous lesson.
options: The revision register from the previous lesson
The sample drawing from the previous lesson
The parts catalogue from the previous lesson
The maintenance checklist from the previous lesson

tasks.prompt: A trainee sent an email about a component that did not match the drawing. The subject line included the part number, and the message described the difference between the drawing and the received item. The trainee attached a photograph and asked the supervisor to confirm the next step. The email avoided blaming anyone and focused on the information needed to resolve the issue. Reading 1. What did the subject line include?
How did the trainee keep the message professional?
options: By omitting the discrepancy from the message
By stating that the supplier made a mistake
By demanding an immediate replacement without evidence
By describing the issue and asking for confirmation without blaming anyone

tasks.prompt: The photograph ___ to the email as supporting information.
Choose TWO features of a clear technical email.
options: A concise description supported by relevant evidence

tasks.prompt: A short line that tells the reader what an email is about is the subject ___.
You need the supervisor to confirm a discrepancy. Which closing request is appropriate?
options: Could you please confirm how I should proceed?
I will make the decision without checking.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of technical email in a logical order.
options: Ask for a clear action or confirmation
correctOrder: Ask for a clear action or confirmation

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words as a technical email reporting a difference between a component and its drawing. Include the reference, evidence and a polite request.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the email identifies the component/drawing reference and describes the observed difference (0–2); it cites evidence and makes a clear, polite request for review or clarification without instructing an unauthorised alteration (0–2); the email has a professional structure and understandable grammar (0–2); drawing/inspection vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
